ns1:channel.ns1:title: Nature Human Behaviour
ns1:channel.ns1:description: Drawing from a broad spectrum of social and natural science disciplines, Nature Human Behaviour will publish research of outstanding significance into any aspect of human behaviour, its psychological, biological, and social bases. How do humans perceive, think, feel, decide, and act? How do they interact with their environments and others? How do these abilities develop and decline over the lifespan? How do they evolve and compare with other species? How do they vary among individuals, groups, and cultures? How are they shaped by socioeconomic and political factors? How are they affected by disease or deprivation? What interventions can influence individual behaviours or outcomes? The journal welcomes research from any discipline that provides significant original insight into these questions.

ns1:item.ns1:title: Selfish and prosocial individuals both distort their actions’ impact, but selfish distortions can be more contagious
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Nature Human Behaviour, Published online: 01 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41562-026-02585-3

In this study, Vollberg and Gross show that both selfish and prosocial individuals exaggerate the social benefits of their choices, with selfish-serving distortions proving to be socially contagious.
ns1:item.dc:title: Selfish and prosocial individuals both distort their actions’ impact, but selfish distortions can be more contagious
ns1:item.dc:creator: Marius C. Vollberg
Jörg Gross
ns1:item.dc:source: Nature Human Behaviour, Published online: 2026-10-01; | doi:10.1038/s41562-026-02585-3

ns1:item.ns1:title: Intrinsic rewards guide visual resource allocation via reinforcement learning
ns1:item.content:encoded:
Nature Human Behaviour, Published online: 01 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41562-026-02573-7

Tangible rewards are known to sharpen visual processing of associated objects. Tomić et al. show that an internal sense of confidence—acting as an intrinsic reward—similarly biases attention, revealing how the brain prioritizes limited resources.
ns1:item.dc:title: Intrinsic rewards guide visual resource allocation via reinforcement learning
ns1:item.dc:creator: Ivan Tomić
Rodrigo Raimundo
Paul M. Bays
ns1:item.dc:source: Nature Human Behaviour, Published online: 2026-10-01; | doi:10.1038/s41562-026-02573-7
